statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) through the CME weekend halt and 12 to 13 (low) in the two scheduled reopen hours; Stress 25 (moderate) now, rising to 47 (elevated) around the reopen; Confidence 61 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in the first twenty-two hours covered here and Tail stays far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs from 25 to 47 as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the reopen and the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence eases from 61 to 48 as the Friday reference tape ages before recovering into the reopen when live price discovery would resume. No danger window is published, because no observed one-way structure exists and none can form while the venue is closed.
headline: Weekend halt, hour 28: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%) closed near the low of a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range, NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, and a post-Jackson-Hole repricing that lifted September hike odds to about 57%; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC inside this window
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, which falls inside this window as its final two slots, so the first twenty-two hours assessed here are a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. The reference tape was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close, finishing near the lower end of that range; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43, down 0.55 percent, within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column, at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year, because the 28 August column has not yet been published; verified Friday reporting places the 10-year about 4 basis points higher near 4.72 percent and the 2-year roughly 8 basis points higher after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks, which markets read as leaning toward a September increase and which lifted odds of a 25 basis point hike to about 57 percent from roughly 35 percent the prior day. That repricing is the single most important item in the current evidence set, and its cross-asset signature is coherent: gold fell 2.88 percent to 4,529.90 dollars, the semiconductor complex led the drag with the Semiconductors group down about 2.9 percent and Semiconductor Equipment down about 4.0 percent, and Technology fell about 1.4 percent. The signature is nevertheless a rotation rather than a broad de-risking, which materially limits the Tail reading: the Dow finished effectively flat at minus 0.02 percent, Communication Services gained about 1.4 percent and Consumer Cyclical about 1.4 percent, and VIX declined on the day rather than bidding. WTI settled near 83.40 dollars, down about 0.16 percent, with weekend reporting continuing to frame the Iran situation as a sanctions and diplomacy confrontation rather than an imminent threat to physical supply, so no geopolitical discontinuity is present in the evidence. Delayed shared cross-asset context was consistent with these verified levels and was used only as confirmation, never as live price-path evidence. Tail is therefore published at 5 for every scheduled halt hour, because the persistent no-retracement path Tail is defined against cannot form in a closed market, and at a conditional 12 and 13 for the reopen hour and the first full hour after it, which allows for a weekend gap on thin Sunday-evening liquidity while remaining far below the 25 block threshold. Stress is published at 25 now and rises through the window to 47 around the reopen, reflecting a genuinely difficult expected environment: an unresolved September policy debate and a dense macro week that runs ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September, ADP and the Broadcom results on 2 September, jobless claims and ISM Services on 3 September, and the August employment report on 4 September. Confidence of 61 reflects a complete and freshly re-verified evidence set whose weakness is age rather than conflict, and it declines to 48 by the final halt hour before recovering as live discovery would resume.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the whole of Saturday 29 August, hours 3 to 26 of the CME weekend halt. The mode was normal in every slot and the mapped policy state never left EA_ON. Tail decayed from 6 to 5 within the first hour and then held the 5 floor for the remaining twenty-three, because no venue was open to produce the price-path evidence Tail is defined against. Stress dipped to a 22 trough in the early hours and then rebuilt to a 25 plateau held for the final eighteen slots, while Confidence declined steadily from 83 to 62 as the Friday reference tape aged without any new observation to refresh it. No slot was unavailable and no assessment in the window was revised with later information.
outlookSummary: The first twenty-two hours of this window fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; Tail is held at 5 throughout, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON, and the dominant mode is normal in those slots because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress climbs from 25 to 44 across those hours as unpriced weekend information accumulates against Friday's hawkish repricing and the dense 1 to 4 September macro week, while Confidence decays from 61 to 48 purely through the ageing of the reference tape. The final two slots are the scheduled Globex reopen at 22:00 UTC and the first full hour after it, the first hours in this window that can host observable structure: they are published with conditional Tail readings of 12 and 13 and a mixed mode, which allows for a weekend gap and thin Sunday-evening liquidity while remaining far below the 25 block threshold, and with Confidence recovering to 55 and 57 as live price discovery would resume. Whether the reopen matters for Tail will depend on whether early retracements hold rather than on the size of any gap, and no such structure is observed or assumed here.
